title: Write every field of an export as the right JSON value

blocks.text: The export service writes each field of an order as a JSON value with `JsonValue.of(...)`. Two kinds of caller use it: code that holds a field in a typed variable (`int quantity`, `char grade`), and code that copies fields from a database row, which arrive as a `Map<String, Object>`. The consumers of the export reject a file in which the same field is written two different ways.

items: whole numbers, decimals and booleans are written unquoted, `12` and `true`, whichever kind of caller passes them;
a single character is written as a one-character string, `"B"`;
text is written quoted, and a missing row field as `null`.

blocks.text: You may add methods to the class. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: whole numbers, decimals and booleans held in typed variables are written unquoted, strings quoted and escaped
a row field that is text is quoted, and a missing one is written as null
a char variable is written as a one-character string, not as its character code
a number or boolean read from a Map<String, Object> is written unquoted, as when it is held in a typed variable

origin.section: Widening First, Then Boxing, Then Varargs: the First Phase That Fits Wins

concepts: A boxed number fits an Object overload by subtyping in the first phase, so it never unboxes to reach a primitive overload.
A char argument widens to an int or long overload in the first phase, before any other overload is considered.
